question: Should Discord orphaned thread sessions be cleaned up automatically, exposed through an explicit agent/operator tool, handled through a Dashboard preview flow, or left to existing manual deletion paths?
rationale: Deleting persistent session rows based on external channel reachability needs maintainer policy for false positives, transcript retention, permissions, and any new config/default surface.

options.title: Preview-first cleanup
options.body: Add plugin-owned orphan detection and a preview/apply flow that revalidates Discord reachability before deleting any session row.

options.title: Agent or operator delete tool
options.body: Expose a constrained deletion or GC action with explicit permissions and auditability, without background pruning by default.

options.title: Keep manual cleanup only
options.body: Decline automatic orphan pruning for now and rely on explicit selected-session deletion or manual repair paths.

recommendation.title: Preview-first cleanup
recommendation.body: Add plugin-owned orphan detection and a preview/apply flow that revalidates Discord reachability before deleting any session row.

likelyOwner.reason: Session maintenance policy and destructive cleanup semantics are closest to the durable conversation-entry preservation and gateway/session control history.
